inspiration: repipe round 2 need xrefs-unify-pe-import; the shape is Ghidra's thunk-function/external-location model, reconstructed from decoded p-code rather than from loader markup

promoted_probe.why: CI has no dataset; the vendored MinGW PE carries the identical defect under the identical import name, count 0 before the fix
promoted_probe.strengthened: count>0 is satisfiable by wrong output, so the promoted clauses pin the two rows to the real call sites (0x140001a9e, 0x140001cce), pin target.name and the disclosed alias, and forbid the veneer's own jmp [slot] from padding the count

speed_method: interleaved child CPU time, min-of-15, with a null control (before vs before) through the same harness; the box carried sibling-agent load, so min is the statistic and the median is reported only to show the noise
speed_note: the cost is the veneer probe: at most 2 extra decodes per decoded function entry, against the hundreds of thousands the walk already does. Query surface only; no decompilation path is affected

sweep.note: every one of the 32 changed entries is a PLT entry; no ordinary function acquired an alias. The 3 increases are each the weak-symbol guard CMP qword ptr [__cxa_finalize@GOT],0x0, a real reference that was invisible before
sweep.pe_note: every aliased PE entry is an IAT slot or an entry whose first instruction is literally JMP qword ptr [slot], verified by disassembly including the 11/18/51-byte ones (those sizes are inventory distances to the next symbol, not bodies)
sweep.byte_identical_surfaces: decompile-all --json, strings --json and decompile-all --reachable-from are byte-identical before/after over pe_imports.exe, aif_gap_x86_64, fauxware, plt_aarch64, macho_imports
sweep.veneer_bound_measured: MAX_VENEER_INSNS=2 and =4 produce byte-identical answers over all 532 queries, so the bound is measured rather than guessed

decisions: The filed hypothesis ('the PE loader creates separate thunk and IAT function records with the same import name, while xrefs are attached only to the IAT record and are not folded across import aliases') is UPHELD as far as it goes, and the record's own hypothesis_status of 'inconclusive' was right to hedge: it describes the second of TWO defects and misses the first, which is not PE-specific at all.

Defect 1 (not in the hypothesis): data_refs skipped in0 for every flow opcode, including BRANCHIND/CALLIND. Those are not static branch targets -- classify files no edge for them -- so the skip lost the reference outright. SLEIGH lifts JMP rm64 as `goto [rm64]`, one BRANCHIND whose in0 is the slot, so EVERY import veneer in EVERY program referenced nothing. CALL rm64 survived only because its constructor spells `local dest:8 = rm64` first and the COPY was scanned. Witness: xrefs --to 0x1400f46c0 (the wcrtomb IAT slot) answered 0 although its veneer at 0x140019960 jumps through it.

Defect 2: the two addresses of one import answered separately, and the failure is symmetric, not thunk-only as filed. On the recorded crackme every call site reads the slot so the veneer reports 0; on the vendored pe_imports.exe `puts` is called through the veneer so the SLOT reports 0. The fix therefore unifies both ways rather than folding the thunk into the slot.

The alias class is derived from the decoded forwarding jump, never from a shared name. Name-based aliasing was the obvious cheap fix and is wrong: pe_iat registers the same name on several addresses, and two unrelated static functions called `init` in different objects would be folded together.

The veneer predicate requires the BRANCHIND's in0 to be a DECODE-TIME CONSTANT data-space varnode. That is what separates a veneer from a jump table -- jmp [rax*8 + table] computes its address and lifts to a LOAD through a temporary -- and it is why the relation needs no PE/ELF knowledge and finds .plt, .plt.sec and .plt.got entries too.

The forwarding jump is excluded from the unified answer, and the first cut excluded it with `function_containing(from) is in the class`. A hand-built unit test caught that as too wide: ordered containment attributes everything after a veneer, up to the next known entry, to the veneer -- so a real caller sitting there would have been silently dropped. The shipped exclusion is the veneer's exact instruction range, which is why Veneer carries `end`.

MAX_VENEER_INSNS was cut from 4 to 2 after measuring: nothing in the fixture corpus needs a third instruction (.plt.sec `endbr64; jmp *GOT(%rip)` and PLT0 `push [got]; jmp [got+8]` are the only two-instruction shapes), and each instruction of slack widens the relation from `this function IS the jump` to `this function ends in one`, which would fold a tail-calling wrapper into the callable it forwards to.

refs_to itself was left alone and the unification added as refs_to_unified, so `kuna strings` and the decompile-all call graph keep reading the per-address buckets. Verified: decompile-all, strings and --reachable-from are byte-identical over five fixtures.

One behaviour change falls outside the need: aif_gap_x86_64's __cxa_finalize now reports the weak-symbol guard read at 0x10ee alongside the call at 0x1102. That is a real reference the query was losing, so the two xrefs_cli tests that pinned the old single-row answer were updated rather than the behaviour narrowed.
Tooling track, so per docs/agents.md a strict wrong-output fix ships with no option, no phases.toml row and no catalog counter -- none were touched, and no counter lease was taken.
